title: Time and condition clauses
point: After if, when, before, after, until and as soon as, use the present tense even when you talk about the future.

sentences.ja: 明日雨が降ったら、家で映画を観よう。
sentences.text: If it rains tomorrow, let's just watch a movie at home.
sentences.note: Say "if it rains", not "if it will rain", for a future condition.

sentences.ja: 駅に着いたら電話するね。
sentences.text: I'll call you when I get to the station.
sentences.note: Use "when I get", not "when I will get"; "get to" is more natural than "arrive at" here.

sentences.ja: 出かける前に電気を消してね。
sentences.text: Turn off the lights before you leave.

sentences.ja: 授業が終わったら図書館に行きます。
sentences.text: I'm going to the library after class is over.

sentences.ja: 彼が来るまでここで待っていよう。
sentences.text: Let's wait here until he shows up.

sentences.ja: 結果が出たらすぐに知らせます。
sentences.text: I'll let you know as soon as I get the results.

sentences.ja: 急がないと終電に乗り遅れるよ。
sentences.text: If we don't hurry, we're going to miss the last train.
sentences.note: Japanese 〜ないと often becomes "If we don't..." in English.

sentences.ja: わからないことがあったら、いつでも聞いてください。
sentences.text: If you have any questions, feel free to ask me anytime.

sentences.ja: 子どもの頃、よくこの公園で遊んだものです。
sentences.text: When I was a kid, I used to play in this park a lot.

sentences.ja: データを集め終わるまで、結論は出せません。
sentences.text: We can't draw any conclusions until we finish collecting the data.
